report.source_text: After consultation with the oncology team, long-acting octreotide 30 mg monthly was suggested. The patient was discharged, but a few days later, he complained from perioral, hand, and feet paresthesia and numbness and developed symptomatic hypocalcemia; his corrected calcium level was 6.5 mg/dl, phosphate level was 2.5 mg/dl, 25 hydroxy vitamin D level was 22.8 ng/ml, and the PTH level was 107 pg/ml. He received intravenous and oral calcium accompanied by 50,000 units of oral ergocalciferol weekly. The symptoms were relieved, and the calcium level was corrected

clinician.trajectory_summary: A 51-year-old man presented with nausea, headache, vomiting, malaise, weight loss, severe hypercalcemia (>15 mg/dl), low PTH, low 25(OH) vitamin D, and acute kidney injury. CT scan revealed a heterogeneous solid mass in the pancreas and multiple hypodense lesions in both lobes of the liver. A percutaneous biopsy of a liver mass confirmed a well-differentiated neuroendocrine tumor (low grade) with positive chromogranin and synaptophysin, and a Ki-67 index < 3%. EUS further characterized the pancreatic mass, showing vascular involvement, and an Octreotide scan showed avid lesions in both the epigastric region (pancreas) and liver, strongly suggesting a pancreatic primary with liver metastases. The severe hypercalcemia was initially managed with IV fluids, calcitonin, hemodialysis, and denosumab. After discharge and initiation of long-acting octreotide, the patient developed symptomatic hypocalcemia, which was treated. Six months later, the patient was readmitted with recurrent severe hypercalcemia and acute kidney injury.

key_supporting_evidence.claim: Patient presented with nausea, headache, vomiting, malaise, weight loss, severe hypercalcemia, low PTH, low 25(OH) vitamin D, and acute kidney injury.
CT scan showed a heterogeneous solid mass in the pancreas and multiple varying size hypodense lesions in both lobes of the liver, with calcifications.

Percutaneous biopsy of the liver mass demonstrated a well-differentiated neuroendocrine tumor (low grade) confirmed by immunohistochemistry (IHC) with strongly positive chromogranin and synaptophysin stain, negative CK20, CK7, LCA, and Ki-67 index of < 3%.

EUS demonstrated a large heterogeneous mass lesion in the body of the pancreas with calcification, measuring 51 mm × 37 mm, with attachment to the common hepatic artery and involvement of the splenic vein. Multiple large heterogeneous mass lesions were also seen in the left lobe of the liver.

Octreotide scan revealed a large donut-shaped octreotide avid lesion in the epigastric region (pancreas) with multiple foci of varying size with abnormally increased radiotracer uptake in the epigastric region and both lobes of the liver.
Severe hypercalcemia was managed with IV fluids, calcitonin, hemodialysis, and denosumab, eventually decreasing to 11.9 mg/dl.

After starting long-acting octreotide, the patient developed symptomatic hypocalcemia (corrected calcium 6.5 mg/dl) with elevated PTH (107 pg/ml), which was managed with IV/oral calcium and ergocalciferol.
Six months later, the patient was readmitted with recurrent severe hypercalcemia (14.4 mg/dl) and acute kidney injury, with low PTH (5 pg/ml).

ruled_out_or_less_likely_alternatives.basis: Initial and recurrent hypercalcemia was associated with abnormally low PTH levels (4.37 pg/ml and 5 pg/ml), ruling out primary hyperparathyroidism as the cause of hypercalcemia.

Immunohistochemistry on the liver biopsy was strongly positive for chromogranin and synaptophysin, and negative for CK20, CK7, and LCA, confirming a neuroendocrine origin and ruling out common epithelial or lymphoid tumors.

remaining_uncertainties: Pathology results of the pancreatic mass biopsy to definitively confirm its nature and primary site of the neuroendocrine tumor.
Direct evidence linking the neuroendocrine tumor to the hypercalcemia (e.g., PTHrP levels, which were ordered but not documented).
The long-term treatment plan for the neuroendocrine tumor beyond initial octreotide, and the patient's overall long-term outcome.
